# tkmt-lab — research lab of Tatsuhiko Takimoto

> Independent research in mathematics and science with AI teams. The first results are on fullerene graphs; later work covers Bell inequalities, analogue Hawking radiation, epidemic-model identifiability and Heesch numbers of polyforms. Each paper is released with a Lean 4 formalization where available, verification data, and a machine-readable claim list stating what has and has not been checked. Checked data sets and tools released without a paper are listed under Data & tools.

## Works

- [Catalog of results (JSON)](https://tkmt-lab.github.io/catalog.json): every published work and claim in one file — stable claim ids, evidence kinds (Lean declarations and axioms, Comparator, independent implementation, AI review, finite computation, numerical evidence, and statement correspondence that does not establish truth), verification commands, DOIs and what is not claimed. Schema: https://tkmt-lab.github.io/catalog.schema.json; explanation: https://tkmt-lab.github.io/catalog.html. Start there, then read the repository's AGENTS.md and run its checks.
- [How the work is checked](https://tkmt-lab.github.io/verification.html): eight reusable verification procedures (frozen statements and Comparator, Lean axiom gates, separately written implementations, certificate checkers, separate AI readers, scope audits, machine-readable claims, correction records), each with what it establishes, what remains, and an example pinned to a published commit. Japanese: https://tkmt-lab.github.io/ja/verification.html.
- [A3 classification of linear gSW paths](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/a3-gsw-classification): GC(k,l)[C20] has a literal linear generalized Stone-Wales path iff an explicit two-stage residue criterion holds. Proved in Lean 4 (standard axioms only), checked with Comparator against an independent statement. Start with AGENTS.md; evidence in packet/claims.json. Current release: tag v1.1.0; Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.23491202 (all versions).
- [Eventual periodicity on affine rays](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/gsw-ray-periodicity): for fullerene families built from a fixed number of convex lattice faces with affine coordinates, existence of a literal gSW path is eventually periodic along every integer affine ray. Main theorem proved in Lean 4 (standard axioms only) for a specification with weaker hypotheses than the paper, checked with Comparator; a prose lemma connects the paper's geometric hypotheses to it. For Graver's family K3(r,s) (two caps of four triangles of side r joined by three hexagons with sides r, r, s, r, r, s) the result on every ray in r, s ≥ 1 and the closed classification (for r, s ≥ 2: a path exists iff s ≡ ±1 mod r) are Lean-proved with no prose step; the same holds for Graver's family C1 (for a, b ≥ 1: a path exists iff b = 1), for Graver's family O2 the ray result and absence of paths for t, d ≥ 2 are Lean-proved with no prose step, and so are the ray result for Graver's family D14 and the classification (r ≥ 2) and ray result for Graver's family E10. For Graver's family D12 the closed classification (for positive r, s: a path exists iff r | s−1, r | s+1 or |r−3s| = 1) and the ray result are Lean-proved (v1.10.0); two earlier computer-assisted proofs are kept as additional evidence. Lean also covers the family arithmetic. Start with AGENTS.md. Current release: see the repository's releases; Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.23491204 (all versions).
- [Bell facet certificates](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/bell-facet-certificates): for the two fixed published lists of C. Staufenbiel — (4,5,2,2) with 49,358 rows and (4,6,2,2) with 4,327,233 rows — every row is a facet of the local polytope, and every row except the single positivity representative of each list is strictly violated by a two-qubit pure state with binary projective measurements given by rational numbers. Two separately written exact verifiers accept every row. Finite evidence concerning Gill's question; no completeness of the lists, optimal quantum values, Lean proof or human peer review is claimed. Full (4,6,2,2) certificates are release attachments. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.23538696 (all versions).
- [Dispersive offset of the analogue Hawking temperature](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/hawking-dispersive-offset): for a one-dimensional flow with quartic superluminal dispersion ω² = k² + k⁴/Λ² and a single horizon, the zero-frequency temperature satisfies T(0)/T_H − 1 = κ g‴(0)/(12Λ²) + O(Λ⁻⁴), with the local coefficient b0 = g‴(0)/(12κ) in derivatives of the flow at the horizon. Formal asymptotic calculation under three stated assumptions (not proved, no remainder bound), supported by full scattering numerics, predictions recorded before calculation, and a separately written scattering code (agreement within about 1e-7). No Lean proof or human peer review. `python3 -B reproduce.py` re-runs everything. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.23553202 (all versions).
- [Global identifiability of a behavioral SIR model](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/behavioral-sir-identifiability): for S' = −βSI/(1+αI)^k, I' = βSI/(1+αI)^k − γI, R' = γI with a fixed known integer k ≥ 2, observed through I(t) with known total population, α, β, γ and S(0), I(0), R(0) are generically globally identifiable — the integer-exponent case of Conjecture 2 of Pant, Saucedo and Pogudin. Prose proof read by two AI reviewers, with exact computer-algebra checks for k = 1..12; no Lean proof or human peer review; non-integer or unknown k and noisy data not covered. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.23553806 (all versions).
- [Heesch number certificates](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/heesch-certificates): for a fixed selection of 3,964 polyominoes, polyhexes and polyiamonds from C. S. Kaplan's tables, every Heesch number (hole-free Hc and outer-holes Hh) equals Kaplan's value and comes with checkable evidence: 6,574 corona witnesses accepted by two geometric checkers (lower bounds) and 5,019 unsatisfiability proofs accepted by drat-trim (upper bounds). Soundness of the SAT encoding on the square, hexagonal and triangular grids is proved in Lean 4 (standard axioms only; Comparator, six kernel runs); the checked CNFs equal the Lean encoding up to renaming by a recorded finite comparison. Also: maximal-corona counts for 22 shapes by two separately written implementations, and a restricted search of 3,442 polyominoes with 20-28 cells that found no finite Hh = 4. The DRAT proofs are checked outside Lean; outer-layer counts have no certificate; the search is not exhaustive; only the listed shapes are covered; no priority or human peer review is claimed. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.23572882 (all versions).

## Data & tools

- [Rooted periodic-net identification tests (RCSR, 1-WL)](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/periodic-net-wl-tests): 99 test cases built from a pinned RCSR-content commit, each a pair of nets with a root vertex in each. Each case records r_min, the smallest radius at which the two rooted balls (all vertices within r edges of the root and the edges between them) are not isomorphic, and r_WL, the smallest radius at which stable 1-WL colour refinement, with initial colours (distance from root, degree in ball), separates them. In 97 cases r_WL > r_min; the largest gap is 4 (tsa V1 / tsg V3: r_min = 4, r_WL = 8). A checker separate from the generator verifies a complete root-preserving isomorphism at r_min − 1 and a non-isomorphism certificate at r_min; the 6 core cases were also computed by a separately written implementation, the other 93 only by this package's checker. Bare graphs only: nothing is claimed about methods that use species, coordinates, distances or angles, about GNNs in general, about radii as numbers of layers, or about a maximum over RCSR (the cases are a selection). No RCSR data is redistributed; the code downloads it and checks its SHA-256. No paper, priority, human review or formal proof. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.23587477 (all versions).

- [Lean statements from published papers](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/lean-statements): 9 Lean files containing 18 theorem statements from 3 published repositories (a3-gsw-classification, gsw-ray-periodicity and heesch-certificates). For readers and programs that want to inspect assumptions, import one statement or find its proof. Definitions, namespaces, hypotheses and types are preserved; every theorem body is intentionally by sorry. Each formal_proof attribute links to a proof at a fixed public commit; research solved marks status. Recorded checks compare the original and local theorem types and inspect metadata. Building this package does not establish mathematical truth or execute the linked proofs. Files with repeated namespaces must be used separately. Not an official part of formal-conjectures and not contributed to it; compatibility with its Lean version and full linter suite is unverified. No new proof or human expert review. Start with AGENTS.md; claims and per-declaration scopes in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.23594152 (this version), doi:10.5281/zenodo.23594151 (all versions).

## Built on

- The question: linear generalized Stone–Wales paths as defined by A. Bille, V. Buchstaber and E. Spodarev ("Some open mathematical problems on fullerenes", 2024/2025).
- The Goldberg–Coxeter construction (named after M. Goldberg and H. S. M. Coxeter; developed for plane graphs, with zigzag theory, by M. Dutour Sikirić and M. Deza).
- J. E. Graver's catalogue of fullerenes with ten or more symmetries; K. Kutnar and D. Marušič on cyclic edge-connectivity of fullerenes.
- The Büchi–Elgot–Trakhtenbrot theorem (monadic second-order logic on words and finite automata).
- For the Bell work: R. Gill's question (Problem 26.B in Krüger–Werner's collection), C. Staufenbiel's sampled facet lists and tools, and S. Lörwald and G. Reinelt's PANDA.
- For the Hawking work: the dispersive analogue-gravity literature, in particular S. Corley and T. Jacobson; W. G. Unruh and R. Schützhold; J. Macher, A. Coutant, S. Finazzi and R. Parentani; U. Leonhardt and S. Robertson; and F. Del Porro, S. Liberati and M. Schneider's effective-horizon result.
- For the epidemic-model work: B. Pant, O. Saucedo and G. Pogudin's question and conjecture; A. Ovchinnikov, G. Pogudin and P. Thompson, and H. Hong, A. Ovchinnikov, G. Pogudin and C. Yap on differential-algebraic identifiability.
- For the Heesch work: H. Heesch's problem; C. S. Kaplan's Heesch numbers of unmarked polyforms, its SAT formulation, dataset and heesch-sat software; C. Mann's survey and C. Mann and B. C. Thomas's computations; A. Fontaine's and B. Bašić's constructions; the Layr-Labs/Eigen Heesch challenge; drat-trim, CaDiCaL, Lingeling, Glucose, PySAT and C. Sinz's sequential counter; C. Codel, J. Avigad and M. Heule's verified SAT encodings.
- For the periodic-net tests: the RCSR database (M. O'Keeffe, M. A. Peskov, S. J. Ramsden and O. M. Yaghi) and the researchers who first described each net; V. A. Blatov and D. M. Proserpio on comparing nets by growing coordination shells; S. N. Pozdnyakov and M. Ceriotti on WL counterexamples for point clouds; O. Delgado-Friedrichs's Gavrog space-group table.
- For the statement collection: the Formal Conjectures Authors, whose file format and category, subject and proof-link attributes it uses (https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/tree/9833012f66a47cdd3a6f3eca9cb4b84e0f18a003).
- Lean 4, mathlib, Comparator and independent Lean kernels.
- Full citations are in each paper or repository.

## Other work

- Novelist: Tatsuhiko Takimoto (滝本竜彦), https://tatsuhikotakimoto.com/en/

## Evidence conventions

- Formal proof, independent derivation, AI review, and finite computation are labelled separately in each claims.json.
- Human peer review and novelty are not claimed unless stated.
- Contact: research@tatsuhikotakimoto.com, or GitHub issues in the relevant repository.
- News and the lab diary: https://x.com/tkmt_lab
